page: Microsoft Azure M96bds_2_v3 is a memory-optimized server belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8473C processor with 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores with 2 threads per core) operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix and integer operations.

The server is equipped with 1946.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 20.27 GB of memory per physical core. It includes 4608 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable, facilitating high-throughput data access. No GPUs are bundled with this configuration. This high resource density positions the server as a robust option for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, offering substantial memory capacity alongside high-speed local storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, with read-only cached small block speeds reaching 7459.57 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 184.54 GB/sec. Multi-threaded performance is strong, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 91198.3 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 559.33 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, scoring in the top tier of Passmark benchmarks with 35122.57 operations, complemented by a Redis SET performance of 114.97 million operations per second. Single-core performance, however, sits in the average tier, indicating that workloads should be optimized for multi-threaded execution to leverage the hardware fully.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M96bds_2_v3 offers a high-density hardware profile that consolidates massive memory and compute resources into a single instance, reducing the overhead of managing multiple smaller nodes. It is highly suited for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, in-memory caching layers, and heavy data-processing pipelines.
